To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) users of realtime transit predictions are uncertain about the accuracy of the predictions, 2) users of realtime prediction systems are not aware of the uncertainty of the predictions, and 3 users of realtime transit prediction systems can be supported by visualizations of uncertainty in the context of the prediction task.

1) users of a popular real-time transit application are often uncertain about the predictions, 2) users of the application have a strong preference for a discrete representation of continuous uncertainty in the form of a dotplot, 3) a discrete representation of uncertainty in the form a quantile dotplot reduces the variance of users' probability estimates by ~1 times compared to density plot and facilitates more confident estimates by users.

1) uncertainty visualizations for everyday, mobile predictive systems should be designed with domain specific requirements in mind, and 2) quantile dotplots are an effective way to communicate uncertainty in the domain of transit predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to visualize uncertainty in realtime prediction systems, and how to do this in a way that aligns with the way that users reason about uncertainty.
how people use uncertainty in the context of everyday mobile systems.
